  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new rule that clears the ETag only runs when the current listing was truncated. A partial `runs_snapshot` that an earlier, pre-fix run cached with a non-null `runs_etag` is therefore still reused after a 304, where `list_runs_for_repo` returns `[], False, response_meta` with `capped=False` and no `page_limit_reached` (line 689). As a result `repo_truncated` is False (lines 2141-2145), the ETag is kept (lines 2268-2274 / 2272-2285), and the partial snapshot is written back to the cache (lines 2284-2287).
  WHY: The coverage report shows the repo as complete: it is missing from `repositories_truncated`, and no `::warning title=Workflow log collection::` annotation is emitted. This repeats on every 304, and for quiet repos over the cap it never ends, which is the failure the P3 fix exists to prevent. The added test covers only fresh truncations. All three flagging reviewers rated it MAJOR (mapped to high). anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 looked at the pass-1 version of this finding and declined to report it, for these reasons: `--max-runs` defaults to 0 and the workflow passes only `--max-pages 50`; page-limit truncation needs at least 1,000 runs; the bug would fix itself on the first change to page 1; and it existed before this PR.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py:`main()` lines 2119–2126, 2141–2145, and 2272–2285 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The ETag change does not recover from partial snapshots that the pre-fix collector already stored. Those cache entries can hold both a truncated `runs_snapshot` and a non-null `runs_etag`.
  WHY: On a 304, `list_runs_for_repo()` reports `not_modified` with `capped=False`. `main()` then reuses the cached snapshot without marking the repo truncated, keeps the ETag, and writes the partial snapshot back as complete, so later reports leave out the collection gap.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py:lines 2119-2126, line 689, lines 2141-2145, lines 2268-2274, line 2287 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The ETag fix stops future truncated listings from caching an ETag, but it does not invalidate partial snapshots cached before the fix. A legacy ETag is sent with `If-None-Match` (lines 672-673), the 304 returns `[], False, response_meta` (lines 687-689), and `main()` reuses the partial snapshot (lines 2120-2126) with `repo_truncated` False (line 2141). It then keeps the ETag (lines 2272-2274) and writes the partial snapshot back (lines 2284-2287).
  WHY: A repo that a pre-fix run truncated at `--max-runs` and that has been quiet since gets a 304 on every collection, so its snapshot is reused as complete forever. The P3 `coverage` object never lists it, no warning annotation is emitted, and the analysis prompt is never told about the data gap.
  NOTE: The reviewer suggests a fix direction. The cache schema (`ai-memory/schemas/workflow_log_analysis_cache.v1.json`) sets `additionalProperties: false`, so no new flag can be stored. On the 304-reuse path, a snapshot with `max_runs > 0` and `len(runs) >= args.max_runs` could be treated as truncated, based on lines 715-717. Legacy snapshots truncated by the page limit cannot be told apart this way and would still need the ETag dropped to force a refetch.
- HARDENING: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py lines 2119-2136 (304-reuse branch in `main()`). A reused 304 snapshot cannot be told apart from a complete listing. Suggested fix: when `args.max_runs > 0` and the snapshot length is at least `args.max_runs`, set `repo_truncated = True`. About 3 lines; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
